newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-EDBERG MAKES TENTATIVE RETURN TO TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG MAKES TENTATIVE RETURN TO TRAINING.

text.p: Stefan Edberg, who hobbled to defeat in Friday's opening Davis Cup final singles after twisting his ankle, made a tentative return to training on Saturday in the hope of playing his final career match on Sunday.

The 30-year-old winner of six grand slam titles, due to retire after the tie ends, jogged five gentle circuits of the court after his doubles team mates had lost their match to Frenchmen Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux.
He then rather gingerly practised some shots, but without exerting himself.
Edberg, who fell awkwardly in the sixth game of his 6-3 6-4 6-3 defeat by France's Cedric Pioline on Friday, has some ligament damage and swelling in his right ankle, his doctor Nils Westlin said.
He kept his foot tightly bandaged after x-rays were taken.
Edberg is scheduled to meet Arnaud Boetsch in the final reverse singles on Sunday, but if he is not fit his place is likely to be taken by Nicklas Kulti, who partnered Jonas Bjorkman on Saturday.
Swedish captain Carl-Axel Hageskog said he would make no decision until just before the matches on Sunday.
